title: AISCORE scorecard v2
description: Two independent axes. Criteria are weighted and scored per interaction. RCM violations are a separate, interaction-level flag that overrides the weighted score entirely. A criterion never carries an RCM category.

category.description: Rollup grouping. Display only - it carries no weight of its own; criterion weights already sum to 1.0 across the whole scorecard.

weight.description: Decimal fraction. All criterion weights must sum to exactly 1.0.

applicable_channels.description: Derive by scanning the FULL behavior text for channel section markers, not the first line. Three criteria in the source rubric open with a 'CHAT' header but contain a later 'VOICE' section, and one carries no marker at all.

expected_behavior_raw.description: Full source text, not yet split by channel. A clean automatic chat/voice split was attempted and rejected: the source text uses inconsistent headers (plain 'VOICE', 'VOICE - OUTBOUND'/'VOICE - INBOUND', or no marker at all), and a wrong automatic split would silently misattribute behavior to the wrong channel, which is worse than not splitting it. Splitting into per-channel fields is deferred to a manual pass, not automated.

automation_method.description: Not in the source rubric. Set per the classifier-discipline rule before wiring this criterion into scoring. 'not_automatable' is a valid and expected answer.

override_type.description: Defined per CATEGORY, not per criterion. Sourced from the 'Scoring reference' sheet. Null means the source rubric never assigned one - see open_questions.

scorecard_version.description: Recorded on every score row so historical scores stay interpretable after a rubric change.

ratings.description: 'na' excludes the criterion from BOTH numerator and denominator. The 0.6 fraction is the source rubric's partial-credit multiplier; it was absent from v1 of this schema, which made the score uncomputable.

partially_meets_gate.note: Policy gate on when the rating may be SELECTED. It is not a per-criterion band available by default. The 0.6 credit above is applied per criterion once the gate is satisfied.

base_score.formula: sum(weight * credit for applicable, non-NA criteria) / sum(weight for applicable, non-NA criteria)

partial_fail.note: Where the calculated score falls below 50%, the lower score stands. A hardcoded 50% cap is the common spreadsheet implementation and would raise a worse score; it is deliberately not used here.

override_precedence.note: Exactly one RCM flag is raised per interaction, at interaction level. It is not attached to any criterion.

category_exceptions.note: Promotes Negligence from partial_fail to auto_zero. The only value-dependent rule in the rubric. Not auto-evaluated in v1; flag for human confirmation.

const: RESOLVED 2026-07-31: Call_Avoidance set to auto_zero (parallels Chat_Avoidance; deliberate avoidance behaviors, not borderline judgment). Sourced from rcm_violations.csv, which is the single source of truth - scoring_engine.py derives its RCM override map from that file at load time rather than hardcoding a copy, so this can't silently drift out of sync again.

RESOLVED: automation_method is now filled in for all 14 criteria in criteria.csv (rule/model per criterion) and is loaded into Criterion.automation_method by scoring_engine.py. It is not yet consumed anywhere downstream to change scoring behavior (e.g. routing 'model' criteria differently from 'rule' criteria) - that wiring is still open, tracked here so it isn't assumed done just because the field is populated and loaded.

expected_behavior_raw/unacceptable_behavior_raw carry the full behavior text per criterion, but are NOT split into per-channel fields - see the field description on expected_behavior_raw for why an automatic split was rejected. A manual pass is needed if per-channel behavior text is required later.

Score output must always be emitted as a number, including on override paths. Spreadsheet scorecards often return a formatted string for overrides and a number otherwise; downstream consumers must not inherit that.
